In this case, the encoded sparse matrix is not being concatenated with the dataframe, so the model is still receiving non-numeric data.

Here is a modified version of the code that correctly concatenates the encoded sparse matrix with the dataframe:


```
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split 
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression 
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder

data=pd.read_csv('/content/toronto\_housing\_data.csv') 

region_encoded = pd.get_dummies(data['region'])
data = pd.concat([data,region_encoded],axis=1) 

encoder = OneHotEncoder()
address_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(data[['address']])

address_encoded_df = pd.DataFrame(address_encoded.toarray(),columns=encoder.get_feature_names_out())
data = pd.concat([data, address_encoded_df],axis=1)
data = data.drop(['address','region'], axis=1)

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(data.drop(['price'],axis=1),data['price'],test_size=0.2) 
model=LinearRegression()

model.fit(X_train, y_train) 
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
```
You will also have to drop the address and region columns from dataframe as it is already encoded and passed in the form of dataframe, Linear Regression model will not accept the string values.
You also have to use encoder.get\_feature\_names\_out() to get the column names for the encoded dataframe.
